paragraphs: Chain Bridge Bancorp, Inc. is a Delaware-chartered bank holding company and the parent of its wholly-owned subsidiary, Chain Bridge Bank, N.A., a nationally chartered commercial bank with fiduciary powers granted by the OCC. The Company was incorporated on May 26, 2006, and the Bank opened on August 6, 2007. The Company conducts substantially all of its operations through the Bank and has no other subsidiaries.

We offer a range of commercial and personal banking services, including deposits, treasury management, payments, loans, commercial lending, residential mortgage financing, consumer loans, trusts and estate administration, wealth management, and asset custody.

Our mission is to deliver exceptional banking and trust services nationwide, blending financial strength, personalized service, and advanced technology to offer tailored solutions to businesses, non-profit organizations, political organizations, individuals, and families. Our vision is to grow responsibly by adapting our personalized service and advanced technology solutions to our clients' evolving needs while emphasizing liquidity, asset quality, and financial strength. We aim to be recognized for our "Strength, Service, Solutions: Your Bridge to Better Banking Nationwide."

As of December 31, 2025, we held total assets of $1.8 billion, including $586.6 million in cash and cash equivalents, of which $580.9 million were interest-bearing reserves held at the Federal Reserve. Our portfolio included $865.4 million in securities, with $527.8 million or 61.0% of that in U.S. Treasury securities. Net loans held for investment, after accounting for deferred fees and costs and allowances, totaled $270.7 million. Our total deposits stood at $1.6 billion, with stockholders' equity at $169.2 million. Approximately 95.3% of these deposits were held in transaction accounts (as such term is defined in the instructions for the Call Report, which the Bank files with the FFIEC on a quarterly basis). Our loan-to-deposit ratio was 17.46%.

Additionally, we hold excess deposits sold one-way to other participating banks through the IntraFi Cash Service® (ICS®). For our clients that opt into the ICS® network, this service allows us to place their deposits in increments up to the FDIC insurance limits at other banks within the ICS® network. In exchange, we may elect to either receive reciprocal deposits from other banks within the ICS® network or place the deposits at other banks as "One-Way Sell®" deposits and receive a deposit placement fee. See "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations — Financial Condition — Deposits" for more information on ICS® deposits.

Chain Bridge Bank, N.A. operates under a national charter with full fiduciary powers granted by the OCC. Our national charter allows us to offer banking services across state lines without additional state banking licenses. The OCC serves as our primary federal regulator, overseeing our operations and compliance with applicable federal banking laws and regulations. Our national bank fiduciary powers enable us to offer trust services broadly.

Our operations under this regulatory framework reflect a banking philosophy that emphasizes liquidity, asset quality, and financial strength. This approach guides our asset allocation strategy, risk management practices, and deposit gathering efforts.

Our balance sheet composition reflects our banking philosophy of emphasizing liquidity, asset quality, and financial strength. We aim to allocate a high proportion of our assets to interest-bearing reserves at the Federal Reserve and to securities that we believe qualify as investment grade.

Our asset allocation strategy is designed to balance liquidity maintenance with income generation. We prioritize investments in securities that we believe qualify as investment grade, with a significant portion allocated to U.S. Treasury securities. This approach reflects our focus on managing credit risk while maintaining liquidity. We strive to maintain a low proportion of assets that we consider to be illiquid.

Our lending policies are designed to manage credit risk. Our approach has historically resulted in what we consider to be low levels of non-performing loans and loan charge-offs. As of December 31, 2025, we have reported no non-performing assets since June 30, 2012. The Company has not reported any loan charge-offs since the third quarter of 2017 and has incurred a cumulative net loan charge-offs of $265 thousand since inception.

We aim to attract transaction account deposits, particularly from commercial clients. Our investment approach for these funds is intended to be conservative, based on our interpretation of prudent banking practices and current regulatory guidelines.
As of December 31, 2025, we served deposit clients in 49 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico.

To support our strategy of attracting commercial transaction account deposits, we emphasize services designed to attract commercial clients who manage high transaction volumes. These services include digital onboarding solutions, image cash letter ("ICL") processing and treasury management offerings that accommodate multiple users with customizable approval hierarchies. This focus aligns with our goal of attracting and retaining commercial clients with complex transactional needs.
At December 31, 2025, 95.3% of our total deposits were held in transaction accounts. For the year ended December 31, 2025, our cost of funds was 0.32%.

headings: Changes in interest rates may adversely affect our earnings and financial condition.
Increases in interest rates have in the past resulted in, and could in the future result in, unrealized losses on our investment securities portfolio.
If the average interest rate we pay on our deposits increases, our cost of funds would rise.
Increases in interest rates could result in a decrease in the market value of our loans.
Liquidity risks could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Loss of deposits could increase our funding costs or require us to sell assets or borrow.
Our deposits are concentrated in political organizations, which can vary significantly in volume due to seasonality or changes in political activity or campaign finance laws.
Our deposit base is concentrated among a small number of clients.
Our deposit base is highly concentrated among entities affiliated with the U.S. Republican Party.
Our deposits are concentrated in uninsured deposits.
Chain Bridge Bancorp, Inc.'s liquidity is dependent on dividends from the Bank.
We may need to raise additional capital in the future, and such capital may not be available when needed or at all.
Our results of operations and financial condition would be adversely affected if the Bank's allowance for credit losses is insufficient to absorb actual losses or needs to be increased.
Losses related to a single large loan could have a significant impact on the Bank's financial condition and results of operations.
Other Risks Related to Our Business
Our business may be adversely affected by conditions in the financial markets and economic conditions generally.

The geographic concentration of our business in the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area makes our business highly susceptible to local economic conditions and reductions or changes in government spending.
paragraphs: The material risks and uncertainties that management currently believes may have a material adverse effect on us are described below. paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read together with our consolidated financial statements and related notes included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. In addition to historical information, this discussion and analysis contains forward-looking statements that involve risks, uncertainties and assumptions that could cause actual results to differ materially from our expectations. Factors that could cause or contribute to such differences include those discussed below and elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, particularly in the section entitled "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" as well as the section entitled "Risk Factors." We assume no obligation to update any of these forward-looking statements except to the extent required by law.

The following discussion relates to our historical results, on a consolidated basis. Because we conduct all our material business operations through our wholly owned subsidiary, Chain Bridge Bank, N.A., the discussion and analysis primarily focus on activities conducted at the subsidiary level.

Chain Bridge Bancorp, Inc. (the "Company") is a Delaware-chartered bank holding company and a publicly traded bank holding company whose Class A common stock is listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "CBNA". The Company was incorporated on May 26, 2006, and is subject to supervision and regulation by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended. The Company serves as the registered bank holding company for Chain Bridge Bank, National Association (the "Bank"), its wholly-owned subsidiary. The Company does not own or control any other subsidiaries and conducts substantially all of its business through the Bank.
We offer a broad range of commercial and personal banking services, including deposit accounts, multiple types of loan products, trust administration, wealth management, and asset custody.

Our mission is to deliver exceptional banking and trust services nationwide, blending financial strength, personalized service, and advanced technology to offer tailored solutions to businesses, non-profit organizations, political organizations, individuals, and families. We aspire to grow responsibly by adapting our personalized service and advanced technology solutions to our clients' evolving needs while emphasizing liquidity, asset quality, and financial strength. We aim to be recognized for our "Strength, Service, Solutions: Your Bridge to Better Banking Nationwide."

In connection with the IPO, on October 3, 2024, the Company filed an Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, which established two new classes of common stock, Class A common stock, par value $0.01 per share ("Class A Common Stock") and Class B common stock, par value $0.01 per share ("Class B Common Stock"), and reclassified and converted each outstanding share of the Company's existing common stock, par value $1.00 per share ("Old Common Stock"), into 170 shares of Class B Common Stock (the "Reclassification"). Share information presented prior to the Reclassification date of October 3, 2024 gives effect to the Reclassification and attributes all earnings to Class B shares because no Class A shares were outstanding prior to the Reclassification.
Highlights of our results of operations and financial condition as of and for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025 are provided below.

•Consolidated net income was $20.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to $20.9 million for 2024. Earnings per share for the year ended December 31, 2025 was $3.08, compared to $4.17 for 2024.

•Net interest income, before recapture of credit losses, was $51.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to $44.4 million for 2024. Net interest income, after recapture of credit losses was $52.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to $44.5 million for 2024.

•Return on average equity was 12.88% for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to 20.05% for 2024. Return on average assets was 1.32% for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to 1.62% for 2024.
•Return on average RWA was 5.28% for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to 5.19% for 2024.2
•Total assets were $1.8 billion as of December 31, 2025, compared to $1.4 billion as of December 31, 2024.

•Total deposits were $1.6 billion as of December 31, 2025, compared to $1.2 billion as of December 31, 2024. Excluded from these totals are One-Way Sell® deposits, which were placed at other banks through the IntraFi Cash Service® ("ICS®") network. These One-Way Sell® deposits amounted to $359.9 million as of December 31, 2025, compared to $63.3 million as of December 31, 2024.
•No non-performing assets or other real estate owned ("OREO") were reported as of December 31, 2025 or 2024.

paragraphs: Chain Bridge Bancorp, Inc. 為一間在特拉華州註冊的銀行控股公司，為其百分之百擁有之子公司 Chain Bridge Bank, N.A. 之母公司，Chain Bridge Bank, N.A. 為一間經美國國庫局（OCC）授予受託人權的全國性商業銀行。本公司於 2006 年 5 月 26 日成立，銀行於 2007 年 8 月 6 日開業。本公司幾乎所有營運均透過銀行進行，且無其他子公司。
我們提供一系列商業與個人銀行服務，包括存款、財務管理、付款、貸款、商業貸款、住宅房貸融資、消費者貸款、信託與遺產管理、財富管理及資產保管服務。

本公司之使命為全國範圍內提供卓越的銀行與信託服務，結合財務實力、個性化服務與先進科技，為企業、非營利組織、政治組織、個人及家庭提供客製化解決方案。本公司之願景為以適應客戶不斷變化的需求為導向，謹慎成長，同時強調流動性、資產品質與財務實力。我們致力於被認可為 "Strength, Service, Solutions: Your Bridge to Better Banking Nationwide."

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司持有總資產 1.8 十億美元，包括 586.6 百萬美元之現金及現金等價物，其中 580.9 百萬美元為存放於美國聯邦儲備系統之利息產生性準備金。本公司之投資組合包含 865.4 百萬美元之證券，其中 527.8 百萬美元或 61.0% 為美國國庫證券。扣除遞延費用及成本與撥備後之應投資貸款總計為 270.7 百萬美元。本公司總存款為 1.6 十億美元，股東權益為 169.2 百萬美元。約 95.3% 之存款為交易帳戶（如該詞項於 Call Report 指南中所定義）之存款，該報告為銀行每季向 FFIEC 報送。本公司貸款對存款比率為 17.46%。

此外，本公司持有透過 IntraFi Cash Service®（ICS®）售出之一方過多存款至其他參與銀行。對於選擇加入 ICS® 網路之客戶，此服務允許我們將其存款以 FDIC 保險額度為限，分批存放於 ICS® 網路內之其他銀行。作為交換，我們可選擇接受來自 ICS® 網路內其他銀行之互惠存款，或將存款存放於其他銀行作為 "One-Way Sell®" 存款並收取存款存放費用。有關 ICS® 存款之更多資訊，請參閱 "管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析 — 財務狀況 — 存款"。
Chain Bridge Bank, N.A. 為一間經美國國庫局（OCC）授予完整受託人權之全國性銀行。本公司之全國性銀行牌照允許我們跨州提供銀行服務，而無需額外州級銀行牌照。美國國庫局為本公司之主要聯邦監管機構，監督本公司營運及遵守適用之聯邦銀行法規。本公司之全國性銀行受託人權使我們能廣泛提供信託服務。
本公司在該監管架構下之營運反映一項強調流動性、資產品質與財務實力之銀行哲學。此方法指導我們之資產配置策略、風險管理作法及存款集資努力。
本公司資產負債表結構反映我們強調流動性、資產品質與財務實力之銀行哲學。我們旨在將資產高比例配置於美國聯邦儲備系統之利息產生性準備金，以及我們認為符合投資等級之證券。
本公司資產配置策略旨在平衡流動性維持與收入產生。我們優先投資於我們認為符合投資等級的證券，並將相當大比例的資產配置於美國國庫證券。此方法反映本公司管理信用風險的重點，同時維持流動性。我們致力於維持低比例的資產，這些資產被我們認為是流動性不足的資產。
本公司貸款政策旨在管理信用風險。我們的作法歷來導致我們認為非放款不良貸款及貸款核銷金額為低水平。截至2025年12月31日，我們自2012年6月30日起已無報告任何非放款不良資產。本公司自2017年第三季起未報告任何貸款核銷，自成立以來累計貸款核銷金額為265千美元。
我們旨在吸引交易帳戶存款，特別是來自商業客戶的存款。我們對這些資金的投資策略旨在保守，基於我們對謹慎銀行作法的解釋及現行監管指引。
截至2025年12月31日，我們在49個州、華盛頓特區及波多黎各服務存款客戶。
為支持本公司吸引商業交易帳戶存款的策略，我們強調設計用以吸引管理高交易量的商業客戶的服務。這些服務包括數位開戶解決方案、影像現金信件（"ICL"）處理及財務管理方案，這些方案可適應多個使用者並具自訂批准階層。此重點與本公司吸引及留住有複雜交易需求的商業客戶的目標一致。
截至2025年12月31日，本公司總存款中95.3%為交易帳戶存款。2025年12月31日財年，本公司資金成本為0.32%。

paragraphs: 下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，應與本年度10-K表報中所包含的合併財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀。除歷史資訊外，本討論與分析包含若干前瞻性陳述，這些陳述涉及風險、不確定性與假設，可能導致實際結果與我們的預期有重大差異。導致或促成此類差異的因素包括下文及本年度10-K表報中其他部分所討論的內容，特別是在「前瞻性陳述警示」與「風險因素」部分。除非法律有明文規定，否則本公司不負有任何更新這些前瞻性陳述的義務。
下列討論與分析涉及我們的歷史營運成果，以合併財務資料為基礎。由於我們的所有重要業務活動均透過我們的 wholly owned subsidiary Chain Bridge Bank, N.A. 進行，因此討論與分析主要聚焦於子公司層面的活動。

Chain Bridge Bancorp, Inc. (the "Company") 是一間在特拉華州註冊的銀行控股公司，並為公開交易的銀行控股公司，其 Class A 普通股於紐約證券交易所上市，代碼為 "CBNA"。本公司於2006年5月26日成立，並受1956年銀行控股公司法案（Bank Holding Company Act of 1956）修正案下美國聯邦儲備系統理事會的監督與管理。本公司為 Chain Bridge Bank, National Association (the "Bank") 的註冊銀行控股公司，為其 wholly-owned subsidiary。本公司不擁有或控制任何其他子公司，並幾乎所有業務均透過 Bank 進行。
我們提供廣泛的商業與個人銀行服務，包括存款帳戶、多種貸款產品、信託管理、財富管理與資產保管。

我們的使命是全國範圍內提供卓越的銀行與信託服務，結合財務實力、個性化服務與先進科技，為企業、非營利組織、政治組織、個人與家庭提供量身打造的解決方案。我們希望以適應客戶不斷變化的需求，透過個性化服務與先進科技解決方案，負責任地成長，同時強調流動性、資產品質與財務實力。我們希望被認可為 "Strength, Service, Solutions: Your Bridge to Better Banking Nationwide."

與IPO相關，本公司於2024年10月3日向特拉華州州務卿提交了修正後的公司章程，設立了兩種新的普通股類別，Class A 普通股，每股面值0.01美元（"Class A Common Stock"），以及 Class B 普通股，每股面值0.01美元（"Class B Common Stock"），並將本公司現有普通股（每股面值1.00美元，"Old Common Stock"）所有流通股份重新分類並轉換為170股 Class B Common Stock（"Reclassification"）。在Reclassification日期（2024年10月3日）前的股份資訊已考慮Reclassification的影響，並將所有盈餘歸屬於Class B股份，因Reclassification前並無Class A股份流通。
我們2025年12月31日財務狀況與營運成果的重點摘要如下。
•2025年12月31日財年合併淨收入為20.2百萬美元，與2024年的20.9百萬美元相比。2025年12月31日每股盈餘為3.08美元，與2024年的4.17美元相比。
•淨利息收入，扣除信貸損失回收前為 51.5 百萬美元，為 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年，較 2024 年的 44.4 百萬美元。淨利息收入，扣除信貸損失回收後為 52.0 百萬美元，為 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年，較 2024 年的 44.5 百萬美元。
•平均風險加權資產報酬率為 5.28%，為 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年，較 2024 年的 5.19%。
•總資產為 1.8 十億美元，為 2025 年 12 月 31 日，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 1.4 十億美元。

其他與本公司業務相關之風險

本公司業務地理上集中於華盛頓特區都會區，使本公司業務高度易受當地經濟條件及政府支出減少或變動之影響。
paragraphs: 本公司管理階層目前認為可能對我們產生重大不利影響的關鍵風險與不確定性，已於下文描述。這些風險因素並非未來結果的保證，應謹慎閱讀，因為它們可能個別或 collectively 對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運結果、流動性、現金流，以及本公司普通股（包括A類普通股）的市場價格、交易量或流動性產生重大不利影響，視情況而定。

此外，這些風險與不確定性並非完整列出，未來可能出現新的或預料之外的風險，或現有風險可能變得更加嚴重，這是因為本公司業務、財務狀況或外部環境的變化，包括但不限於經濟、法規、政治、科技與市場環境。任何於下文所描述的風險，以及目前尚未為本公司所知、目前認為不具重大性，或未來可能變得具重大性的其他風險，可能個別或 collectively 對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運結果、現金流，以及本公司A類普通股的交易價格、波動性或流動性產生重大不利影響，不過這些影響的發生、時間或影響程度無法確定。

進一步而言，若本年度報告表10-K中任何資訊屬前瞻性陳述，則下列風險因素旨在作為1995年私人證券 litigation 改革法案（"PSLRA"）、1933年證券法第27A節（已修正）及1934年證券交易所法第21E節（已修正）所定義的警示性陳述，識別某些可能導致實際結果與任何前瞻性陳述中所表達的結果有重大差異的關鍵因素。前瞻性陳述本質上涉及內在風險與不確定性，本公司無法保證我們的預期、預測或假設會證明正確，或任何特定結果會發生。投資人應謹慎勿過度依賴任何前瞻性陳述，因為實際結果可能因本公司控制內外因素而大幅變動。請參閱「關於前瞻性陳述的警示性說明」以取得這些限制的更多細節。
